question: A contractor employs 15 men to complete a work in 24 days, working 8 hours per day. After six days, he adds five more men but also reduces the working hours to six per day from the seventh day onwards. If all men work with the same efficiency throughout, how many more days will be required to finish the remaining work?
solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Equating remaining work directly using the MDH rule: M₁ × D₁ × H₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂ Remaining work for 15 men would take 18 days (24 − 6) at 8 hours/day. For the new group of 20 men (15 + 5) working at 6 hours/day, the required days is D₂. 15 × 18 × 8 = 20 × D₂ × 6 ⇒ 2160 = 120 × D₂ ⇒ D₂ = 18 **∴ The correct answer is 18 days.**
